items.title: Precision Medicine Using Artificial Intelligence and Genomics: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Precision medicine is an emerging healthcare paradigm that tailors prevention, diagnosis, and treatment to individual patients using genetic, clinical, environmental, and lifestyle information. Advances in next-generation sequencing, bioinformatics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) now allow clinicians to analyse genomic variants, stratify disease risk, and select therapies at a level of individual detail that population-averaged medicine cannot provide. This paper reviews AI-enabled precision medicine, synthesising landmark and recent peer-reviewed literature published between 2004 and 2026, and tracing the field from early blood-group stratification through the Human Genome Project to national precision medicine programmes and the multimodal AI of the present day. A conceptual framework is proposed that integrates electronic health records, genomic sequencing, laboratory tests, and wearable-device data in a secure platform where AI models identify biomarkers, predict risk, and recommend treatment for clinician validation; it is synthesised from literature-reported practices rather than experimentally validated. Applications in oncology, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, rare genetic disorders, pharmacogenomics, and remote monitoring are examined, followed by the main challenges, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, unrepresentative genomic datasets, cost, interpretability, and ethics, together with mitigation strategies. Emerging directions, including digital twins, federated learning, multimodal AI, and CRISPR-assisted therapies, are discussed. This review highlights the role of AI and genomics in moving healthcare from reactive to predictive and personalised, and identifies priorities for future research.

items.title: Predictive modeling and multi-objective optimization of 3D-printed PLA parts using a hybrid random vector functional link (RVFL) and henry gas solubility optimization (HGSO) framework
items.abstract: To forecast the mechanical characteristics of 3D printed Polylactic Acid (PLA) specimens, this work explores artificial intelligence models. Tensile strength (TS) and surface roughness (Ra) of printed parts were examined in relation to five process parameters: build angle (BA), infill angle (IA), layer thickness (LT), printing speed (PS), and nozzle temperature (NT). In the machine learning modelling stage models such as Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), Random Vector Functional Link tuned by Henry Gas Solubility Optimization (RVFL-HGSO), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) were created to forecast the printed parts’ surface roughness and tensile strength. Moreover this study shows the effectiveness of random vector functional link model tuned by the Henry Gas Solubility Optimization (RVFL-HGSO) when predicting surface roughness. The developed model achieved highest R2 = 98.95%, RMSE = 0.777, MAPE = 1.002%, and MAE = 0.514 on test dataset. It increased R2 by 4.98% when compared with RVFL and by 9.93% when compared with ANN on test dataset. RVFL-HGSO decreased MAPE by 49.93%, also MAE by 53.90%, and RMSE by 29.68% when compared with RVFL on test dataset. It also, decreased MAPE by 69.02%, also MAE by 73.95%, and RMSE by 58.49% when compared with ANN. The multi-objective optimization by particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) gives best possible solution at place of BA = 44.16, NT = 220, IA = 14.93, LT = 0.22, PS = 45.18: Minimum predicted Ra = 2.53 and maximum predicted TS = 44.15. The findings demonstrate the RVFL-HGSO model’s unique method for finding intricate correlations in the dataset, laying the groundwork for better product design and mechanical property optimization through process parameter adjustment.

items.title: Predictors of Lower Back Musculoskeletal Disability Among Emergency Department Healthcare Professionals: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs), particularly lower back (LB) pain are highly prevalent in emergency department (ED) healthcare professionals with significant health-related impacts due to the high and unexpected workload. Objective: This study aimed to identify the predictors of LB disability among ED healthcare professionals in Jordan, including physical, psychological, and ergonomic occupational factors. Methods: A multicenter convenience sample of ED healthcare professionals was recruited from Jordanian ED departments. Data collection included demographics, ergonomics-related factors and a group of validated outcome measures: the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21). A stepwise multivariable linear regression model was used to identify predictors of LB disability. Results: The study included 447 participants, of whom 57% were male ( n = 255) and had a mean age of 35.1 ± 7.0 years. Predictors of the ODI ( R 2 = .31) included depression ( B = 0.456, p < .001), taking sick leave in the past 12 months (β = 6.8, p < .001), safe handling and posturing practices ( B = −5.584, p < .001), age ( B = 0.32, p < .001) and presence of musculoskeletal injury in the past 12 months ( B = 4.6, p = .022). Conclusion: This study highlights the burden of LB disability among ED healthcare professionals. LB disability was significantly associated with depression, recent Musculoskeletal injury, Musculoskeletal-related sick leave and older age, with safe handling and posture practices showing a protective effect. items.title: Preparation and Outlook for the Era of Solo Entrepreneurship: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework for Artificial Intelligence Service–Centered Startups
items.abstract: The proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) now enables individuals to develop and operate services that formerly required the resources of entire organizations, creating a distinct wave of solo entrepreneurship centered on AI services.This study defines AI-based solo entrepreneurship as venture creation in which one founder, without cofounders or employees, designs, builds, and operates a market offering by embedding AI tools as core productive capacity rather than peripheral aids.It analyzes how this transformation unfolds and identifies the capabilities and challenges founders must prepare for.Drawing on an integrative review of domestic and international literature and a structured, criteria-based analysis of documented AI-based solo-venture cases, the study distinguishes success determinants from the barriers founders commonly encounter.The analysis identifies three capabilities most associated with success-proficiency with AI tools, digital marketing capability, and a disposition toward continuous learning-and recurrent barriers of psychological resistance to technology, funding difficulty, weak marketing and sales capability, and isolation and burnout from working alone.Building on these findings, the study proposes an integrated analytical model that cross-examines success factors and barriers across four dimensions-capability, resources, market, and psychology-and derives a four-stage strategy (preparation, execution, growth, and scale-up) with policy tasks in education, institutions, and finance.Because the model is conceptually derived rather than empirically validated, it is advanced as a set of testable propositions rather than confirmed results.This study contributes by specifying concretely the preparations required of individuals, firms, and government and situating its integrated model against established entrepreneurship frameworks to assess its distinct contribution.

items.title: Preparing Modernisation Decisions of Public IT Recruitment through a Semi-Automated NLP Approach to Mapping Gov-ernmental Syllabi onto ESCO and e-CF
items.abstract: The rapid digitalisation of public services and the emergence of artificial intelligence, data science, and cybersecurity have exposed limitations in existing competency frameworks for public-sector IT professionals. In Spain, the long-standing examination syllabus for Level A IT civil servants is undergoing reform to address the growing misalignment between assessed competencies and current professional requirements. This paper presents a semi-automated, human-in-the-loop process to support decision-making by mapping the existing syllabus and authoritative European professional profiles to two complementary frameworks: the European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations (ESCO) taxonomy and the European e-Competence Framework (e-CF, EN 16234-1). The pipeline uses Sentence-BERT (S-BERT) with MPNet-based embeddings and cosine similarity to identify relevant skills and competences. Before automated matching, specialised profiles in artificial intelligence, data science, and cybersecurity, including references published by the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), are harmonised using consistent ESCO and e-CF terminology. The resulting candidate profiles are ranked for stakeholder consideration and consolidated through expert validation. By combining semantic matching, multi-source harmonisation, and expert judgement, the proposed approach reduces complex information to a manageable set of profiles, supporting decisions on candidate selection and competency development in public-sector IT. The methodology provides a replicable approach for modernising public recruitment in alignment with European competency frameworks.

items.title: Preservice Teachers' Perceptions of Digital Platforms: Insights into Moodle and AI Apps for Lesson Planning and Delivery
items.abstract: Preservice teachers are increasingly integrating technologies such as Moodle and AI-driven (artificial intelligence) applications into their pedagogical preparation; however, their attitudes toward these tools remain underexplored. The study examined preservice teachers' perceptions of digital platforms: insights into Moodle and AI apps for lesson planning and delivery. The study adopts the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) as its theoretical framework. A qualitative research approach was employed, utilising an interpretive phenomenological design to examine preservice teachers' lived experiences and attitudes in depth. The population comprised 243 preservice teachers enrolled in a Bachelor of Education program at a South African university. A purposive sample of 12 participants was selected, ensuring representation across year levels and subject specialisations based on their exposure to digital platforms. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews. Data analysis followed Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis process, using NVivo software, which involved familiarisation, code generation, theme development, and review for rigour. The study findings revealed that preservice teachers described Moodle as highly useful for collaborative lesson planning, praising its resource-sharing features for fostering peer feedback and organisation in group projects. The study concluded that preservice teachers hold largely favourable attitudes toward digital platforms, affirming their role in competency development. However, there are still gaps in AI familiarity, highlighting the need for teacher training. These attitudes align with TAM predictions, understanding the need for intentional integration. The study recommends embedding Moodle and AI modules in preservice curricula and providing hands-on workshops to boost confidence and address barriers.

items.title: Prevalence of and factors associated with work-related musculoskeletal disorders among orthopedic nurses: a cross-sectional study with exploratory interpretable machine-learning modeling
items.abstract: Objective This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of musculoskeletal symptoms and work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) among orthopedic nurses, identify demographic, occupational, and lifestyle characteristics associated with WMSDs, and explore whether routinely collected characteristics could discriminate nurses with WMSDs from those without. Method A single-center cross-sectional study was conducted among nurses at a tertiary orthopedic specialty hospital in China between March and November 2023. Conventional analyses included multivariable logistic regression, modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors, and negative binomial regression. Logistic regression as a benchmark, elastic-net logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and support vector machine were compared using repeated 5-fold cross-validation with fold-specific preprocessing. Prediction performance was assessed using AUC with bootstrap 95% CIs, PR-AUC, Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, and descriptive threshold metrics; TreeSHAP was used for model interpretation. Result Among 948 nurses with valid questionnaires, 654 reported musculoskeletal symptoms in the previous 12 months, irrespective of work attribution (68.99%). After excluding 44 participants with uncertain work-related attribution, 604/904 participants were classified as having work-related WMSDs (66.81%). Each 1-point increase in the strict ergonomic risk score was associated with WMSDs in logistic regression (adjusted OR = 2.631, 95% CI 2.039–3.432; p < 0.001) and modified Poisson regression (adjusted PR = 1.283, 95% CI 1.203–1.369; p < 0.001). The highest observed AUC was 0.752 (95% CI 0.721–0.791) for the domain random forest model; the domain XGBoost model had the highest PR-AUC (0.841). Conclusion Musculoskeletal symptoms and WMSDs were common among orthopedic nurses in this single-center sample. Occupational exposure and postural load were associated with WMSDs. The exploratory prediction models showed limited-to-moderate discrimination and warrant prospective multicenter external validation before practical application.

items.title: Privacy, AI, and Social Media Platforms
items.abstract: The right to privacy in Africa remains underdeveloped within the African Union legal framework, with the Banjul Charter containing no explicit privacy provision. Simultaneously, artificial intelligence has fundamentally transformed privacy dynamics through social media platforms’ unprecedented data collection. This chapter examines the normative status of privacy in Africa and identifies pathways for strengthening protection against AI-driven violations. It first documents how AI’s dependency on data, coupled with surveillance capitalism’s business models, creates novel threats: platforms exploit the ‘privacy paradox’ (the gap between users’ expressed concerns and their actual data-sharing behaviour) to collect vast quantities of personal information, with African users particularly vulnerable given limited privacy literacy. It then assesses the regulatory framework: international human rights law recognises privacy as fundamental, but the Banjul Charter’s silence creates a normative gap that fragmented national data protection laws cannot fill. The Malabo Convention represents significant progress, though questions remain regarding the distinction between privacy and data protection. Finally, the chapter explores interpretive and regulatory pathways to strengthen privacy protection against AI-driven threats while maintaining coherence with regional human rights obligations.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Produtividade líquida no empreendedorismo individual: quanto a IA economiza depois da revisão e do retrabalho? Ensaio teórico com proposições e agenda de pesquisa
items.abstract: The most widespread promise of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for solo entrepreneurs is time savings. Experimental evidence documents substantial gains on well-defined tasks, but large-scale adoption studies find modest self-reported savings, and at least one randomized trial with experienced professionals found an increase, rather than a reduction, in completion time. This theoretical essay argues that part of this discrepancy stems from conflating gross productivity — the time saved in generating an output — with net productivity — the time and value saved after accounting for task specification, verification, correction, rework, context switching, and the expected cost of errors that escape review. For solo entrepreneurs, this distinction is especially relevant because the same person generates, reviews, corrects, and answers for errors, with no division of labor to absorb these costs. Integrating the economics of productivity and time allocation, the literature on quality costs and rework, research on automation and overreliance, human–AI interaction studies, and recent empirical evidence on GenAI at work, we propose an accounting model of net productivity, with explicit cost components and boundary conditions, and derive eight propositions. We discuss implications for solo entrepreneurs, limitations, and a study design with task-level randomization and an illustrative power calculation. The article presents no empirical data; its propositions are intended for testing.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

items.title: Program-wide approaches to changing assessment in response to GenAI
items.abstract: Given the rapid development and increased availability of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), adapting assessment so that it builds student GenAI literacy and assures student learning in scalable and sustainable ways is imperative. In this chapter, we discuss different approaches that can be taken to address the need to change assessment in response to GenAI. We also present a case study of one potentially scalable and sustainable way to address this challenge, a program-wide approach adopted to review assessment across three health programs in response to GenAI. Team members received GenAI professional development; all assessment tasks in core units were then mapped, and collaborative discussions undertaken within teams to identify key opportunities within the program to both build student GenAI literacy and minimise the impact of GenAI on assuring learning. Assessment changes were then made. The chapter then outlines the affordances and challenges of this program-wide, collaborative approach to redesigning assessment given the impact of GenAI, and discusses undertaking program-wide assessment change in response to GenAI.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

items.title: Programmable Auxetic Metamaterial‐Based E‐Skin for Conformable Dual‐Mechanism Spatiotemporal Sensing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT While self‐powered flexible e‐skins based on nanogenerators hold immense promise for wearable electronics, severe interfacial mechanical mismatches occur under complex joint deformations, limiting reliable multichannel sensing. Herein, a 4D‐printed mechanical metamaterial‐enabled e‐skin with an auxetic scaffold and AI‐assisted decoding is developed to improve deformation accommodation and support multichannel sensing during joint motion. Benefiting from an auxetic architecture with a tunable negative Poisson's ratio (−0.41 to −1.76), the metamaterial skeleton expands laterally under stretch to mimic the strain‐stiffening behavior of biological tissues. By concentrating local stress, this geometrical programmability transforms the skeleton into an active mechanical amplifier, significantly boosting the triboelectric‐piezoelectric (TENG/PENG) responses. An integrated nine‐channel array captures these amplified spatiotemporal features with high fidelity. During fast running, the device yields robust 3 V outputs and resolves 3 Hz rhythmic motions. Further, by introducing a lightweight 1D convolutional neural network (1D‐CNN) to decouple intricate spatiotemporal crosstalk, the system achieves advanced motion‐state classification with an exceptional accuracy of over 95% on average across different tasks. This integration of mechanics and artificial intelligence offers a robust platform for next‐generation intelligent wearable rehabilitation and human‐machine interfaces.
topics: Advanced Sensor and Energy Harvesting Materials

items.title: Prompt engineering as an extension of information literacy: Implications for library instruction programmes
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now a routine information tool for students and knowledge workers, and the quality of what they obtain depends in part on how they instruct it. This article argues that prompt engineering is best understood as an extension of information literacy, and that library and information professionals should lead its teaching in partnership with other units. Using conceptual analysis, it maps prompt competencies onto the six frames of the ACRL Framework for Information Literacy for Higher Education and, unlike earlier mappings, identifies where the analogy fails. The mapping holds for question formulation, evaluation and refinement. It fails where a language model generates text and does not retrieve documents, where its sources cannot be inspected, and where it fabricates citations. Those failures are the strongest argument for librarian involvement, because they call for verification skills that prompt technique alone does not supply. The article proposes an instructional design in four strands, including one for workplace settings, sets out how each can be assessed, and considers equity of access to instruction. It also addresses two objections: that prompt engineering is a transient skill, and that librarians are not yet prepared to teach it. The argument is conceptual and requires empirical evaluation.

items.abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming modern healthcare by enabling autonomous decision-making, adaptive learning, and real-time patient monitoring. Unlike conventional AI systems with static rule-based behavior, agentic AI can reason, plan, and act proactively using multimodal health data. This paper presents an AI-driven system designed to support early diagnosis, improve patient engagement, and enhance medical decision-making. The system integrates Flask-based web technology, autonomous reasoning agents, and interactive analytics to predict potential diseases based on user-entered symptoms. Experimental evaluation demonstrates fast response time, high usability, and promising diagnostic performance. Challenges such as privacy, dataset limitations, and clinical validation are discussed. Overall, the work provides a scalable framework for intelligent healthcare support systems.

items.title: Recent Developments in Intelligent, Active, and Sustainable Food Packaging Systems for Enhanced Food Safety and Quality Assurance
items.abstract: ABSTRACT: Background: The global food packaging industry is undergoing a paradigm shift from passive containment toward dynamic, multifunctional systems that actively preserve food quality, monitor spoilage in real time, and minimize environmental impact. Objectives: This review synthesizes recent advances (2020–2025) in intelligent, active, and sustainable food packaging with emphasis on technological principles, material innovations, and regulatory frameworks. Methods: A comprehensive narrative review was conducted using peer-reviewed literature from PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. Publications from 2020 to 2025 were included. Results: Active packaging incorporating antimicrobial agents, essential oils, and nanocomposites demonstrated significant shelf-life extension. Intelligent systems including colorimetric freshness indicators, time-temperature indicators (TTIs), biosensors, and RFID-enabled labels offer real-time food quality data. Sustainable alternatives such as polylactic acid (PLA), chitosan-based films, and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) address environmental concerns associated with petroleum-derived plastics. Artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) integration are accelerating these advances. Conclusion: Convergence of smart materials, digital technologies, and circular economy principles is transforming food packaging. Harmonized regulatory frameworks, consumer acceptance, and cost-effectiveness remain critical challenges for broader adoption. Keywords: active packaging; sustainable food packaging; nanocomposites; biosensors; food safety; shelf-life extension; biopolymers.

items.title: Reclaiming Human Innovative Intelligence and Agency in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) has changed the economics of information retrieval, synthesis and idea generation. It has not, however, eliminated the need to decide which problems merit attention, which assumptions constrain inquiry, which conclusions are justified by evidence and which futures should be pursued. This paper argues that human innovative capability should be deliberately developed alongside AI deployment. It introduces the Meta-Box as a heuristic for examining nested assumptions at the levels of task, process, system, purpose and underlying human need. It then proposes a Human Innovation Lab: a reproducible, evidence-informed training environment combining disciplined curiosity, assumption interrogation, analogical transfer, radical problem reframing, intelligent dissent, structured human–AI cooperation and experimental verification. The proposal is critically situated against Creative Problem Solving, design thinking, TRIZ, Synectics and related methods. The published creativity-training literature provides qualified support for trainability, but methodological weaknesses and limited evidence of long-term workplace transfer preclude strong efficacy claims. Accordingly, a falsifiable research program is specified, including blinded assessment, active comparators, unfamiliar transfer tasks and longitudinal workplace outcomes. The paper advances a normative and empirical proposition: the value of AI will be greater when organizations cultivate people capable not merely of obtaining answers but of discovering, challenging and reconstructing the questions that govern action.

items.title: Reclaiming judgement. Arendt and the ethical transformation of pedagogy in AI-mediated education
items.abstract: This paper examines the ethical transformation of pedagogy in the age of artificial intelligence through the framework of Hannah Arendt’s concept of judgement. It argues that algorithmic systems may erode teachers’ and students’ capacity for moral agency, fostering instead what Arendt diagnosed as thoughtlessness. Drawing on postdigital theory, the paper shows how automated decision-making increasingly replaces reflective deliberation with procedural compliance. Against this, the paper proposes treating algorithmic outputs as a starting point for ethical reflection. It concludes that reclaiming judgement is essential to sustaining education as a domain of moral engagement.

items.title: Reconstructing Teacher Agency in the AI Era: A Proposal for the Dynamic Pedagogical Autonomy Model (DPAM)
items.abstract: The present research endeavors to delineate a model for the positioning of teacher autonomy and curricular agency as generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly integrated into the educational ecosystem. Adopting a qualitative document analysis design, the study systematically scrutinized strategic policy frameworks from the OECD (2026), UNESCO (2025), and the European Union AI Act (2021). This analysis culminated in the development of the three-layered Dynamic Pedagogical Autonomy Model (DPAM), a framework designed to resolve the inherent ontological tension between technological velocity and the human essence of pedagogy. Findings indicate that the temporal efficiencies afforded by GAI in instructional planning and preparation act as a crucial time capital, thereby providing educators with the professional space required to exercise and develop their projective agency. Yet, as underscored by the model’s layers of Critical Pedagogical Filtering and Social-Emotional Interaction, neither the relational core of education nor legally mandated human oversight can be effectively substituted by GAI systems. Ultimately, the research frames GAI not as a threat of automation, but as a hybrid intelligence partner that bolsters the teacher’s epistemic authority and professional autonomy.

items.title: Regional Specificities of AI Adoption
items.abstract: The relevance of the study is due to the implementation of the national project "Data Economy and Digital Transformation of the State," which has identified a pronounced spatial unevenness in the regions of the Russian Federation, requiring the systematization of regional models for the implementation of AI (artificial intelligence) and the identification of factors that determine the success of digital transformation in territories. The purpose of the study is to identify significant factors of interregional asymmetry in the implementation of regional policy in the field of AI, to determine the types of regional models of digital transformation of regions, and to develop recommendations for improving the effectiveness of a differentiated approach at the level of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. To achieve this goal, the authors analyzed the regional conditions for AI implementation using the example of five territories. The scientific and practical significance of the work lies in the development of a typology of five regional AI models and in substantiating the direct correlation between the level of infrastructure development and the digital maturity of the region. Key findings of the study : it has been established that the most successful model is a systemic one, combining a high level of institutional maturity, large scale implementation of AI projects, and long-term planning of human resources potential; it has been demonstrated that “blind” replication of successful practices in regions with a different economic structure and budgetary capacity is ineffective; the key problem areas of the regional AI implementation policy have been identified: digital inequality, a shortage of interdisciplinary personnel, barriers to scaling up scientific developments, and infrastructure constraints; the need to move from unified approaches to a differentiated regional policy has been substantiated, taking into account the level of digital maturity, budgetary capacity, and infrastructure development of each constituent entity. Conclusions of the study : a transition from unified approaches to a targeted, differentiated AI implementation policy is required, taking into account the level of various development metrics of the territories. It is necessary to strengthen individual support for depressed regions through the development of human resources potential and the institutional environment. The success of digital transformation is determined not by the volume of funding, but by the region’s ability to integrate effective management mechanisms, which requires a revision of the budgetary approach to resource allocation and methodological support for the territories.

items.title: Regulatory Technology Regtech Transforming Compliance With Intelligent Systems
items.abstract: Regulatory compliance is constantly evolving challenge for organizations, particularly in highly regulated industries like finance and healthcare. Manual, fragmented, and traditional compliance processes are inefficient, error-prone, and costly, increasing the risk of potential harm. Regulatory technology (RegTech) helps ensure compliance through smart solutions such as automation, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and data analytics. This chapter discusses how RegTech automates compliance processes to ensure data accuracy and reduce human intervention. Using AI and ML, RegTech systems can analyze regulatory data, detect threats, and ensure compliance with changing regulations in real-time. This makes them flexible and responsive to changing regulations. This chapter discusses how RegTech improves data privacy and security which minimize the impact of data breaches and regulatory fines.

items.title: REIMAGINING EDUCATION: PROSPECTS AND CHALLENGES OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE UTILISATION AMONG HENSARD UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
items.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence into higher education has necessitated a growing reliance on this technologyby students in tertiary institutions. This has raised concerns about academic integrity and the cultivation of essentialscholarly attributes, like critical, analytical skills and attitudes towards problem-solving. Existing scholarshipemphasises artificial intelligence’s technical potential and institutional integration, with less attention paid to students’experiences, motivations, and the challenges of everyday academic use. This study examined the prospects andchallenges of artificial intelligence utilisation among Hensard University students, in order to provide evidentiarybases that will help in reimagining teaching, learning, and assessment in the Nigerian educational system. Guided byartificial intelligence adoption and digital dependency theories, the study adopted a qualitative survey design, drawingon Focus Group Discussions with twenty-one students purposively selected. A semi-structured Focus Group InterviewGuide was used for data collection. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings indicated that theextent of artificial intelligence utilisation among Hensard University students was high. Further findings showed thatstudents perceived artificial intelligence as beneficial for enhancing academic performance, enabling personalisedlearning, and developing 21stcentury skills. Major challenges identified included overreliance on artificial intelligence,academic dishonesty, reduced critical thinking, and limited digital literacy. The study concluded that while adoptionwas driven by perceived benefits, unmanaged dependence can undermine the very learning outcomes artificialintelligence was meant to support. The researchers recommended among others that, tertiary institutions in Nigeriashould develop clear guidelines on the acceptable use of artificial intelligence in students’ assessments.

Reimers, whose scholarship has long focused on comparative analysis of educational models (Reimers, 2000; Reimers & Tiburcio, 1994; Vincent-Lancrin et al., 2022). items.title: Reinforcement Learning Approaches to the Dynamic Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: This systematic review analyses how Reinforcement Learning (RL) applied to the Dynamic Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (DFJSSP) contributes to industrial production systems, considering problem formulations and extensions, algorithm families and scheduling strategies, and scalability. ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, Taylor & Francis and Web of Science databases were searched between November 2025 and January 2026, using eligibility criteria requiring RL as the primary method, explicit modelling of dynamic events, experimental validation, and quantitative instance data. A total of 231 records were identified, from which 43 studies were included. Results show that 21 studies incorporate additional resources, such as transport and energy and human factors. The review shows that PPO and DQN approaches account for 37% and 35% of studies respectively, with single-agent architectures prevailing in 65% of cases. It was identified that most studies focus on small-scale to medium-scale simulated instances, and heterogeneous parameterisation of dynamic events limits cross-study comparability. In addition, this review characterises the sustainability dimensions (economic, environmental and social) addressed by RL approaches to the DFJSSP, based on the optimisation objectives adopted in each study. Future research should jointly address economic, environmental and social objectives with explicit indicators and validate RL on real industrial data to establish it as an enabler of sustainable manufacturing in DFJSSP.

items.title: Rekonstruksi Kehadiran Pastoral di Tengah Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence dalam Pelayanan Gereja
items.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence has changed the pattern of communication and ministry of the church, including the practice of pastoring in virtual spaces. This research aims to reconstruct the concept of pastoral presence in the AI era and formulate a pastoral model that remains rooted in the relational and spiritual character of Christian ministry. The research uses a library research method with a theological-contextual qualitative approach through a literature analysis on pastoral theology, digital pastoral, and AI in church life. The results of the study show that AI can expand and strengthen pastoral ministry, but it cannot become a pastoral subject or replace human relations. This research offers a Relational–Spiritual–Ethical–Transformative Pastoral Presence model, which places relationality as the foundation, spirituality as orientation, ethics as boundaries, and transformation as the goal of pastoring.

items.title: Relevance and Applicability of the Master of Arts in Educational Management Curriculum to Graduates' Professional Work: Basis for Curriculum Enhancement
items.abstract: Higher education institutions are expected to continuously evaluate graduate programs to ensure that curricular offerings remain relevant, responsive, and aligned with the evolving demands of professional practice. This study assessed the relevance and applicability of the Master of Arts in Educational Management (MAEM) curriculum of Guagua National Colleges to the current professional work of its graduates and identified areas for curriculum enhancement. Using a quantitative descriptive-comparative research design, data were collected from 33 MAEM graduates through a structured survey questionnaire. Descriptive statistics such as frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and ranking were utilized to analyze quantitative data, while thematic analysis was employed to examine graduates' recommendations. Results revealed that most graduates occupy positions closely related to educational leadership and management, with 87.88% indicating that their present work is highly related or related to educational management. The overall relevance and applicability of the curriculum obtained a very high rating (M = 4.69), while the adequacy of competencies developed through the program received a mean rating of 4.67. Human Resource and Organizational Management emerged as the highest-rated competency area (M = 4.76), whereas Problem-Solving and Evidence-Based Decision-Making obtained the lowest mean rating (M = 4.64), though still interpreted as very high. Graduates recommended strengthening content related to digital leadership, educational technology, artificial intelligence, instructional leadership, research utilization, and experiential learning. Based on these findings, a Responsive MAEM Curriculum Enhancement Framework was proposed. The study concludes that the MAEM curriculum remains highly relevant to current professional requirements but should continuously evolve to address emerging educational challenges and technological advancements.

items.title: Research on the Dynamic and Communication Mode of Public Opinion Emotions Based on Text Mining and Sentiment Analysis
items.abstract: The swift dissemination of public opinions on university-related events is inevitably associated with topic variations, emotions, and complicated interpersonal interaction among the users. To explore this problem, this study proposes a hybrid framework including text mining, sentiment analysis, and opinion evolution modeling based on fuzzy theory. Data about public opinions will be collected on social platforms like Weibo, Douyin, and Xiaohongshu, then will be subjected to data cleaning, Chinese word segmentation, and stop-word elimination. An optimized version of BERTopic is employed to detect topics by means of domain knowledge mapping, keyword pre-exploration, topic labeling via assistance of large language models and fine-tuning of embedding models. Sentiment tendencies will be further divided into types with help of a model that combines RoBERTa-BiLSTM and interactive attention and biaffine feature fusion. Based on these analyses, a fuzzy opinion-evolution model is built to evaluate the impact of peer trust, opinion leader trust, timely and credible responses on emotions and consensus. A case of university cafeteria-related public opinion event will be adopted for empirical analysis. The findings indicate that the proposed framework can identify theme and emotion variations in campus public opinion. Higher opinion leader trust can speed up inter-group consensus while too much reliance on peer interactions may delay it. Late and low credibility responses are likely to increase public opinion risk.

items.title: Research Progress and Clinical Translational Application of Ultrasound Localization Microscopy in Microcirculation Imaging
items.abstract: Abstract As an emerging super-resolution ultrasound imaging technology, ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) breaks the acoustic diffraction limit of conventional ultrasound. By localizing and tracking individual microbubble contrast agents at the sub-wavelength scale, ULM achieves high-precision visualization and quantitative evaluation of micron-level microvascular structures and hemodynamic parameters. Compared with traditional color Doppler flow imaging and contrast-enhanced ultrasound, ULM possesses superior spatial resolution and microcirculation quantification capability, enabling in-depth analysis of microvascular morphological remodeling and functional perfusion abnormalities. This review summarizes the core technical principles, optimized algorithms, and key technical bottlenecks of ULM, including microbubble signal separation, single-bubble localization accuracy, physiological motion artifacts, and prolonged acquisition duration. Furthermore, we comprehensively elaborate the preclinical and clinical application progress of ULM in multiple systems, covering neurovascular, renal, tumor, cardiovascular, endocrine and cardiac microcirculation diseases, with a specific focus on its novel clinical value in identifying vulnerable carotid atherosclerotic plaques. We also discuss the current limitations restricting large-scale clinical translation, standardized protocol establishment, and deep-tissue imaging performance of ULM, noting that the majority of existing human ULM evidence is still at the feasibility stage and large-scale prospective multi-center clinical validations are still needed. Targeting the above-mentioned translational bottlenecks, finally, this review prospects the future development directions of ULM, including artificial intelligence optimization, three-dimensional whole-organ imaging, multi-modal and multi-omics fusion. With continuous technical iteration, ULM is expected to become a novel non-invasive imaging modality for early diagnosis, risk stratification and therapeutic efficacy evaluation of microcirculation-related disorders.

items.title: Reskilling and Upskilling in the Age of Intelligent Automation
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of intelligent automation technologies - encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and robotic process automation (RPA) - is fundamentally reshaping the global workforce landscape. This chapter examines the critical imperatives of reskilling and upskilling as strategic responses to technological displacement and the evolving demands of the labor market. Drawing on contemporary empirical research and theoretical frameworks, the chapter explores how organizations, educational institutions, and policymakers can collaboratively design and implement effective workforce development interventions. Special attention is given to the role of lifelong learning, digital literacy, and human-centric competencies in sustaining employability. The chapter also addresses equity dimensions, highlighting disparities in access to training opportunities across demographic and socioeconomic groups. Practical models and evidence-based recommendations are provided for building resilient, future-ready workforces capable of thriving alongside intelligent machines.

items.title: Rethinking e-business through AI: comparative insights and actionable solutions
items.abstract: Purpose The incremental adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has been emphasized in much academic research and still remains incomplete with regards to the context-based acceptance and utilization. Prior studies mainly focused on technological acceptance and organizational growth but most of the time they overlook the constraints between economy-wise or country-wise differentiation in AI adaptation. To fill this gap, this paper adopts a comparative framework that integrates Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) & Dynamic Capability View (DCV) to analyze the dimension of AI adoption in e-business. Design/methodology/approach We adopt the systematic process of peer-reviewed articles within 2020–2025 to find the similarities and differences in adoption drivers across the developed and developing economies. Findings Findings reveal that TAM based factors like perceived usefulness and ease of use triggers user behavior and intention (high vs low adoption) in developed and emerging economies while the DCV factors such as sensing, seizing and reconfiguring are fully utilized by organization in developed countries where reconfiguration is obstructed in emerging economies because of resources, regulation and skills scarcity. Originality/value This study contributes by adopting a comparative framework with theoretical implication that not just explains the economic dimension in AI integrated e-business, rather provides a holistic idea of influence for user-level and organizational-level capability.

items.title: Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer OCT Quality Assessment: Comparing General-Purpose and Clinical AI Tools Using Global and Stepwise Prompting
items.abstract: As interest grows in multimodal large language models (LLMs) for ophthalmic imaging, their reliability must be established before clinical use. A key prerequisite is determining whether image quality permits interpretation. However, their ability to assess retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) optical coherence tomography (OCT) scan quality remains uncertain. We compared a general-purpose AI tool (ChatGPT-5.1) with a clinical AI tool (DoxGPT) for RNFL OCT report-quality assessment. Both evaluated 145 bilateral reports from 11 patients in an enriched quality-control sample using global and stepwise prompts. One ophthalmologist’s responses to the same predefined quality questions served as the clinical reference for calculating percent agreement, linearly weighted Cohen’s κ with patient-level cluster-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted κ (PABAK). Global prompting showed higher observed agreement than stepwise prompting: ChatGPT, 56% versus 47% (κ = 0.36 [95% CI, 0.23–0.49] versus 0.12 [0.08–0.18]); DoxGPT, 59% versus 48% (κ = 0.41 [0.28–0.54] versus 0.13 [0.03–0.23]). Component agreement was higher for signal strength (ChatGPT/DoxGPT: 99%/99%) and optic nerve head centering (87%/96%), and lower for dropout (41%/43%) and segmentation error (64%/65%). Both tools showed limited agreement with the ophthalmologist for overall RNFL report reliability. Their accuracy requires independent validation, supporting continued clinician review.

items.title: Retomando explicaciones con un chatbot por IA
items.abstract: The expansion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) poses new challenges for higher education, particularly in Ibero-American contexts where empirical evidence remains scarce. This article presents an exploratory study analyzing the pedagogical use of an educational chatbot, based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, developed and implemented at the Universidad Nacional de Río Negro (UNRN) in Argentine Patagonia. The system converts transcriptions of recorded lectures into a navigable semantic corpus, which allows 57 students to query the teaching discourse accumulated throughout the course. The study adopts a longitudinal mixed-methods design that combines quantitative analysis (of 355 messages recorded across 40 sessions) with qualitative analysis (of student interactions). The architecture is documented in a detailed and reproducible manner: n8n orchestration, Whisper transcription, OpenAI embeddings and generation, top-20 dense retrieval over a Pinecone vector database, and conversational memory in PostgreSQL. On this basis, the expected performance of its components and their sources of error are discussed. The conceptual framework articulates situated learning theory (Lave & Wenger, 1991) with the theory of conceptual fields (Vergnaud, 1990, 1996); this perspective emerged from the analysis of the data itself. Drawing on the empirical evidence and the architectural analysis, the category of augmented pedagogical memory is proposed as a conceptual tool for describing longitudinal RAG infrastructures closed to the pedagogical corpus. The results show a predominant use oriented toward conceptual clarification, procedural reorganization, and the recapitulation of situated content, with no expansion toward external frameworks.

items.title: Return to purpose
items.abstract: We identify that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has given rise to numerous public debates and academic scholarship. These reactions often highlight the threats GenAI poses to assessment practices and, by extension, the long-term implications for universities’ ability to provide quality education and trusted credentials. We position these responses along a continuum, from those who advocate a return to tightly controlled onsite examinations to those who claim that the presence of GenAI renders traditional examinations futile and obsolete, and who see this moment as an opportunity to free the university from the ‘shackles’ of assessment and credentialing altogether. In this chapter, we engage critically with the latter position. This chapter employs critical speculative methods and presents a dystopian-oriented vignette in which the university loses its relevance as a credential-granting institution. We identify and discuss three key dimensions in which higher education needs to engage critically with GenAI: (i) how AI reshapes disciplinary knowledge across fields; (ii) how it transforms university teachers’ work environments; and (iii) how widespread GenAI use might affect student capabilities. We aim to raise critical questions for institutions, educators, and policymakers about GenAI’s brutal irruption into higher education and potential consequences on assessment practices.

items.title: Revolutionizing Healthcare: Healthcare 4.0 for Advanced Disease Detection and Treatment
items.abstract: Using cutting-edge technologies, Healthcare 4.0 transforms the identification and treatment of diseases in the human body. Diagnoses may be made more successfully and precisely with this paradigm shift, partly because of big data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI). AI algorithms analyze a variety of medical data, including genetic information and clinical imaging, to find patterns and anomalies, enabling the rapid and precise identification of diseases. Additionally, remote monitoring and wearable technology allow for continuous health surveillance, alerting medical professionals to 82 anomalies and facilitating fast intervention. Healthcare 4.0 also places a lot of emphasis on personalized medicine, which tailors treatments to individual variations utilizing genomic sequencing and molecular profiling. Telemedicine and virtual care have also become crucial since they enable remote consultations and reduce the need for in-person visits. Healthcare 4.0 equips medical professionals with the tools to use data-driven diagnostics (DDD) and other technologically supported methods to increase patient care, boost treatment outcomes, and better diagnose diseases.

items.abstract: Draft technical note and reproducibility package prepared for Arcforth. RFQ-30 contains 30 AI-assisted synthetic procurement intake cases: ten complete, ten incomplete and ten conflicting. Two deterministic extraction baselines were executed. The first-value baseline matches 230/240 annotated fields but releases ten conflicting requests; the duplicate-aware baseline matches 236/240 fields and still releases four prose-conflict cases. These are descriptive results on a constructed fixture, not operational error estimates. The package includes data, reference labels, code, actual per-case outputs, a frozen local protocol, a data card and limitations. No LLM model was evaluated, no human review time was measured, and no client data or outcomes are included. AI assistance was used in authoring and analysis. Guía práctica para micro y pequeños negocios formales en Colombia (persona natural con RUT o sociedad, con hasta 10 trabajadores) sobre obligaciones legales que suelen descubrirse solo ante una sanción, una demanda o un siniestro. Revisa ocho frentes: datos personales (habeas data), ciberseguridad y fraude digital, seguridad y salud en el trabajo, trabajadores y contratistas, impuestos y obligaciones con la DIAN, registro mercantil y socios, propiedad intelectual, y publicidad y protección al consumidor. Cada sección parte de una situación real y explica qué exige la norma, cómo aparece el riesgo y qué hacer este mes. Cierra con un autodiagnóstico de 22 preguntas, con la evidencia que respalda cada respuesta, para elegir las tres primeras acciones. Las normas y cifras se verificaron en fuentes oficiales entre el 27 y el 29 de octubre de 2026. La guía no reemplaza la asesoría profesional: cada negocio es distinto. Palabras clave: microempresa; mipymes; cumplimiento normativo; gestión de riesgos; protección de datos personales; seguridad y salud en el trabajo; obligaciones tributarias; emprendimiento; Colombia. Abstract. A practical guide for formal micro and small businesses in Colombia (sole proprietors or companies with up to 10 employees) on legal obligations that are often discovered only when a penalty, a lawsuit or an incident occurs. It covers eight areas: personal data protection, cybersecurity and digital fraud, occupational health and safety, employees and contractors, tax obligations, commercial registration and partners, intellectual property, and advertising and consumer protection. Each section starts from a real-life situation and explains what the law requires, how the risk appears and what to do this month. It closes with a 22-question self-assessment, with the evidence supporting each answer, to choose the first three actions. Rules and figures were checked against official sources between 27 and 29 October 2026. The guide does not replace professional advice. Written in Spanish. items.title: Robotic-Assisted Surgery: A Comprehensive Review of Applications, Advancements, Limitations, and Future Directions
items.abstract: This narrative review evaluates the evolution and clinical impact of robotic-assisted surgery across the principal surgical specialties, including urology, cardiothoracic surgery, neurology, gynaecology, orthopaedics, and gastrointestinal surgery. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched for English-language publications from January 2000 to August 2026. The retrieved literature was synthesised narratively by specialty; no standardised quality appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, meta-analysis, or certainty-of-evidence grading was undertaken, and all quantitative estimates are reported as published by the cited sources. Studies that met the inclusion criteria were analysed across procedure-specific robotic techniques, clinical and technical outcomes, and specialty-specific applications. The findings demonstrate substantial but uneven advancement across specialties. In urology, robotic-assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy reduced intraoperative blood loss by 60–70% relative to open surgery and shortened hospital stay, without demonstrated oncological superiority. National registry data from the United Kingdom (2024), France (2022), Taiwan (2011–2024), and China (2024) report urology at 43–61% of national robotic procedure volume, in datasets that differ in scope, denominator, and observation period, with general surgery dominant in United States da Vinci platform volume. In neurology, a 2024 meta-analysis of 15 studies (732 patients) reported a pooled vector error of 1.09 mm for robot-assisted deep brain stimulation. In orthopaedics, 2023–2025 meta-analyses confirm improved mechanical alignment in robotic total knee arthroplasty but equivalent functional outcomes and implant survivorship. In gastrointestinal surgery, a meta-analysis of 72 studies (30,081 patients) reported lower conversion, reduced blood loss, and improved overall survival for robotic gastrectomy at the cost of longer operative time. Across specialties, robotic assistance most consistently reduces blood loss and, in anatomically demanding fields, conversion to open surgery, and improves ergonomics, although the size of these benefits varies by procedure; however, longer operative times, higher costs, and the absence of haptic feedback remain unresolved, and the evidence base for long-term oncological and functional benefit is still maturing.

items.title: Role and Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Libraries: Challenges and Future Prospects in the Digital Age
items.abstract: Libraries around the world are being transformed with Artificial Intelligence. AI has had a major impact on libraries ability to provide services more effectively, more accurately, and more widely than previously thought possible. AI encompasses a variety of technologies used by libraries, such as machine learning, chatbots, natural language processing, robotics, and recommendation systems. This enables libraries to provide readers with more efficient, accurate, and accessible ways to access information, and helps librarians develop book catalogs. This study explores the use of AI in libraries, assesses the impact of AI on library operations and services, identifies challenges in implementing AI in libraries and explores the future of intelligent libraries. Methodologically, this research used a descriptive, analytical approach based on an extensive literature review of books, peer-reviewed articles, conference proceedings, scholarly publications and relevant websites related to AI and library and information science. In addition to increasing efficiency of the library system as an entity, the use of chatbot technology for engaging with library users on a personal level will also greatly improve user experiences by making it easier for them to engage with library operations as well as providing them with personalized services. Finally, throughout the course of this paper, the concluded that AI has changed the way many people perceive libraries as they become more intelligent and give users new and better access to information while keeping them as a priority in how they are being serviced. In order for libraries to successfully implement and continuously utilize AI solutions, there is a need for overcoming existing technological and organizational structures.

items.title: Safe, Fluent, and Culturally Thin: Generative AI as a Medium of Postcolonial Visibility Across the Lusophone World
items.abstract: Large language models can generate fluent text in many languages, but fluency reveals little about how well they distinguish the cultural worlds that share a language. This article asks what kinds of cultural differences GPT-4o makes visible across eight Lusophone countries and whether greater visibility also produces culturally grounded representation. The study compares 1680 cross-cultural jokes generated under a safety-oriented prompt and a specificity-seeking prompt across 56 directed country pairings. Explicit cultural marking rose from 20.0% to 64.3% and increased in 54 pairings, showing that target visibility is strongly prompt-sensitive. The added markers were generally accurate, although unevenly distributed and often drawn from a limited repertoire of recognizable signs. No joke contained a recoverable source-country voice, while historical relations and culturally situated perspectives remained rare. Greater cultural marking did not bring greater semantic repetition: visibly marked outputs were no more repetitive in meaning. Prompting therefore made targets more recognizable without recovering a culturally situated speaking position. Histories and relations connecting the Lusophone countries largely remained outside the generated humor.

items.title: Safety Culture as a Socio-Technical Phenomenon
items.abstract: Safety culture is a determinant of organizational performance in high-reliability industries, yet research on it has stayed divided between technical and cultural traditions. This chapter conceptualizes safety culture as an irreducibly socio-technical phenomenon. It draws on socio-technical systems theory, James Reason's organizational accident model and Swiss Cheese Model, and the ICAO Safety Management System. The model positions safety culture at the intersection of human, process, technology, and structure, where it is both an outcome of system design and a mediating variable that regulates how systems respond to complexity and failure. The chapter transfers this to Industry 4.0, where cyber-physical systems, artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things restructure the human-machine relationship. Aviation's experience with cockpit automation, fly-by-wire systems, and Crew Resource Management is a longitudinal reference. The chapter closes with transferable principles: just culture, integration of human factors into system design, and continuous learning.

items.title: Same automation pressure, divergent outlooks: human resource development deficits associated with the stagnant employment outlook for Korean pharmacists in the age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are reshaping the health workforce, yet projected employment differs across professions. The 2025–2035 qualitative job outlook published by the Korea Employment Information Service categorizes occupations using mean annual employment changes from its 2023–2033 quantitative projection. These changes are +2.7% for nurses, +1.9% for physicians and dentists, +1.7% for radiological technologists, +1.6% for Korean medicine doctors, +1.5% for clinical laboratory technologists, and +0.5% for pharmacists. Pharmacists alone among these seven professions are categorized as maintaining their current employment level, a downgrade from the previous edition. The outlook lists AI-driven automation as a decreasing factor for nurses, radiological technologists, and clinical laboratory technologists as well, although their projected growth remains positive. This narrative review combines policy and document analysis, an analysis of the national health insurance fee schedule effective 1 September 2026, and a comparison of pharmacy curricula to examine institutional characteristics that may help explain this divergence. Three interrelated features of pharmacist human resource development (HRD) are identified. First, 257 of 281 community pharmacy billing codes (91.5%) are dispensing fees tiered by days’ supply; medication counseling is the sole explicitly cognitive service among the six pharmacy fee categories. Second, professional development infrastructure was established later than for physicians and nurses, and a national specialist pathway for community practice is planned but not yet operational. Third, the extension of pharmacy education to six years substantially expanded experiential training, while school-based preparation remains limited in the curricula examined. No objective comparison of the outcomes of four- and six-year graduates was identified in this review. These features may help explain the divergence but have not been shown to cause the employment projection. An HRD agenda linking professional development, remunerated services, community specialization, and AI competencies is proposed.
